title: Introduction to CNC Programming and Operation; Mill
description: This CNC programming and operations course is an introduction to mill tool path programming using G & M code format, including CNC systems and components and machine controller functions and operations. The focus of this course is to introduce students to program entry, editing, verification, calculation for mill cutter compensation, cutting tool selection and basic mill setups. Demonstrations of workholding and precision inspection techniques will also be included in this course.
outcomes: Demonstrate the set up and basic operation of vertical machining centers.
Create basic word-address programs to successfully construct projects using vertical machining centers.
objectives: Describe three axis CNC milling machines.
Select and calculate logical tool paths and positioning for mill cutters.
Prepare basic three-axis programming for milling machine operations
Operate mill CNC controller to download and dry run part programs
Describe mill setup procedures for work piece and fixture offsets
Apply the use of precision measuring tools to inspect the accuracy of machined parts
Describe mill cutting tool materials; characteristics, and uses.
Explain the common types and characteristics of CNC milling machine tooling.
content: Describe three axis CNC milling machines.
CNC milling machine types and applications.
One inch tape and floppy disks (historical reference).
Word address, EIA/ISO standardized alphanumeric codes.
X, Y, and Z axis designations.
A, B, and C rotary axis designations.
Continuous path, contouring, linear and circular interpolation.
Select and calculate logical tool paths and positioning for mill cutters.
Effective rough, semi-finish and finish cuts for productivity and accuracy.
Close tolerance and thin wall applications.
X and Y for symmetrical and non-symmetrical parts.
Right triangle laws: computing unknown sides and angles; conversion of minutes/seconds to decimal degrees and decimal degrees to minutes/seconds; scientific calculator operation.

Calculation of cutter compensation: definition of point, line, angle and arc; plot coordinate points for mill cutters (to form inside/outside square obtuse and oblique corners)(to form inside/outside corners with 90 degree arcs).
Prepare basic three-axis programming for milling machine operations
Circular interpolation: with I and J; with R.
Plunge milling methods: pre-drill; straight plunge or ramp.
Verify CNC programs by means of machine simulators and software verification tools.
Operate mill CNC controller to download and dry run part programs
Down load programs from PC or DNC.
Down load programs from USB drive.
Use jog functions to accurately locate spindle.
Call up and run programs in memory.
Run tool tryout with single block and adjusted feed rates.
Describe mill setup procedures for work piece and fixture offsets
Location and setting of workpiece/fixture zero.
Apply the use of precision measuring tools to inspect the accuracy of machined parts
Describe mill cutting tool materials; characteristics, and uses.
Explain the common types and characteristics of CNC milling machine tooling.
lab: Explain multi - axis CNC milling machine
Demonstrate CNC mill set up procedures
Identify measuring tools and inspection techniques
Setup CNC milling tooling (cutting tools and holders)
assignments: Lab projects demonstrating mastery of skills using three axis CNC machines, simulators and verification software covered in this course.
Take home and in class worksheets involving feeds, speeds, and cartesian coordinate calculations.
